verdict.rationale_short: Markets were closed July 11 (Saturday). The HOLD from July 10 carries forward with all regime gates intact: SPX 7,575.39 (115pts above the 7,460 dual-gate floor), VIX 15.84 (well below 17). Two significant catalysts land this week: (1) Monday July 13 — SKHY begins regular trading; 50% allocation authorized at open per the July 9 protocol (SKHYV closed $168.01, above the $162 constructive threshold); (2) Tuesday July 14 — triple-event stack: June CPI at 8:30am ET (consensus headline -0.2% MoM / ~3.9% YoY, driven by June's 21% oil price decline during the Hormuz-reopening window; core +0.22% MoM / ~2.9% YoY), Fed Chair Warsh congressional testimony (Fed revised 2026 inflation forecast to 3.6%), and mega-bank earnings pre-open (JPM, BAC, GS, WFC, C; options pricing 4-6% implied moves with NIM as the key metric). Per the July 9 protocol, CPI ≤3.5% YoY upgrades HOLD to BUY. Consensus at 3.9% does not hit the trigger — the upgrade requires a meaningful beat of consensus. Trump's ceasefire-'OVER' declaration from July 10 has not yet translated into WTI above $80 (current ~$75 WTI / $79 Brent); the 2-4 week Hormuz inventory-impact lag means June CPI is clean but July CPI will absorb any oil disruption signal. BTC holding $63,944 Saturday night (Gate 2 at $62K intact by ~$1,944). Do not chase SKHY above $175 pre-CPI or NVDA above $215 ahead of the Tuesday binary.

bear_case: The bull case for Monday July 13 rests on two concurrent catalysts — SKHY's debut and NVDA's authorized full-size add — both executing on the assumption that Tuesday's CPI will deliver relief. That stacking is precisely the bear case: if Monday brings institutional buying into SKHY open and NVDA add, and Tuesday's CPI print fails to beat consensus meaningfully (consensus 3.9% vs. the protocol's ≤3.5% BUY trigger), then the intraday reversal on July 14 could come when positions are fully committed. Kiplinger warns explicitly: the expected -0.2% MoM headline is 'misleading' — it is entirely a function of June's oil price decline during the Hormuz-reopening window, which Trump has since declared closed. Core CPI at +0.22% MoM / 2.9% YoY remains sticky. Fed Chair Warsh testifying against the backdrop of a revised 3.6% 2026 inflation forecast is unlikely to validate the rate-cut narrative that a soft headline might prompt. The bank earnings (4-6% implied moves) stacked on the same day as CPI and Warsh testimony create a volatility corridor where any one of three inputs can dominate price action. The DAL template is live: beat on fundamentals, sell off 4%. If CPI lands at 3.9% consensus (not a beat), Warsh sounds cautious, and one major bank guides softly on NIM compression, VIX could spike back toward 17 and the 115-point buffer above the 7,460 dual-gate floor gets tested. Counter-argument: if CPI prints 3.7% or lower (below consensus), the September hike probability collapses from ~60%, Warsh has less runway to sound hawkish, and the bank earnings become less consequential. That outcome resolves HOLD → BUY at high conviction and the SKHY 50% → full allocation upgrade clears.
